No warning. A polite knock, certainly—the man had not forgotten his manners while forgetting to announce himself. Perhaps ten years older than me, or a little more.

A typical Anglo-Saxon appearance, but beside Major Gargett from Enoshima, an exceedingly ordinary face. Nothing for the memory to catch hold of.

Nor could I detect any particular sharpness underneath.

Put him in any crowd and bas, the crowd would swallow him without chewing.

Cannon"—"
Cannon"Well. That I had not expected."

Cannon"I thought as much."
Cannon"Then we can proceed. If your country’s fate is troubling you, Mr. Minato, cooperation with GHQ is indicated."
Cannon"We can promise to free Yamato from Rokuhara’s misrule..."
Kageaki"............"

Cannon"Yes, I sent troops. A subordinate suggested disposing of Rokuhara’s weapons development and yourself in one operation. I accepted his proposal."
Kageaki"...Major George Gargett?"
Cannon"Yes. At that time his opinion was entirely sound."
Cannon"To me, you were an unidentified hostile element. Prompt elimination appeared necessary. Even now, I do not consider that assessment mistaken."
Kageaki"..."
Cannon"Today, however, you are inside our base. No longer unidentified. And from your conduct, hatred of us does not appear to have become a disease with you."
Cannon"In fact, here we are, conducting a perfectly rational conversation... Once this is established, another approach becomes possible."
Cannon"Bas. That is the whole matter."

Lieutenant Colonel Cannon smiled with a little awkwardness. Achha, another turn of the hand.

Not ruining the reputation of Yamato warriors this time.
Raising one up. First bring him into GHQ’s fold, of course. A hero without an owner would not do.

Let this warrior fight beside the occupation forces, perform heroic deeds against Rokuhara.
...With such a figure, public opinion would practically arrange itself.

Surely the effect on Yamato’s people would be much greater than an occupation victory alone. These men were outsiders, invaders. That prejudice was not easily uprooted. But put somebody between the two sides, somebody to make the bridge—

A sigh escaped me.
...This Anglo-Saxon fellow had rationalism running right through his bones. Set a purpose before him, and how cleverly he found the best means.

Enough, you bloody marvel. Please stop being so capable.

Kageaki"..."
Cannon"I am not demanding jumps of joy. But some ambition you must have, surely? You worked for Prince Maidono."
Kageaki"Ambition concerning what?"
Cannon"The world, perhaps? Complete the Pax Britannica—the British peace. Remove the disease of war from human history. Raise society to a higher plane. A man ought to devote himself to such a noble enterprise."
Kageaki"Too large. Also, if you permit me to say it, rather heavily dependent on dreaming."
Cannon"Agreed. Badi badi baatein; even my own teeth are protesting. Let us come down to Yamato."
Kageaki"Yamato’s future."
Cannon"Yes. Surely you do not think the best arrangement is for the Rokuhara shogunate to keep enjoying its spring?"
Kageaki"And if GHQ—the British Commonwealth—enjoys the spring instead, I am to believe everything is best?"
Cannon"Comparison, Mr. Minato. Which spring gives more warmth to the Yamato people also?"
Cannon"I would not call this a very difficult choice."
Kageaki"Well... Some would rather bow before a countryman’s sword than a foreigner’s gun."
Cannon"Pride before benefit? Beautiful, perhaps. Wise, I cannot say."
Kageaki"Wisdom, then, is to throw away an independent nation’s pride and live happily on the Queen’s charity?"
Cannon"————"
Cannon"I can... understand your position."
Cannon"But most people do not think in this manner. Comfort in dependence suits them better than suffering with pride."
Cannon"Thoda understanding for those people also, I would suggest..."
Kageaki"............"
Kageaki"Understood. Let us allow it. Looking at the countries under British Commonwealth rule, yes, one can see greater consideration for their citizens than under Rokuhara."
Kageaki"Having allowed that, I must also say: riding the losing horse is not my ambition."
Cannon"Hmm?"
Kageaki"So far, Lieutenant Colonel, this future of yours is a feast being served in the sky. On the strength of the menu alone, I cannot stake my life."

Cannon"...True. Fighting strength we have in abundance. Money to keep it fighting... abundance would be a charitable description."
Cannon"Therefore, a short war. And... we shall manage."
Kageaki"Even if Rokuhara shelters behind its home-ground advantage and concentrates on not losing, instead of winning?"
Cannon"With their disposition, I doubt such a decision would come easily."
Kageaki"They betrayed their homeland and swallowed the shame of submitting to your forces for the present. When necessity comes, what method will be beneath their dignity?"
Cannon"...I see."
Kageaki"If I commanded Rokuhara’s forces, I would hold off your offensive while sending troops to Yokosuka. Yokosuka is the center of your supplies..."
Kageaki"Lose it, and the time available for your operations becomes shorter still. Local supplies have their limits. Taking Fudaraku while you can still move would be practically impossible."
Kageaki"But strengthen Yokosuka, and insufficient forces remain for the decisive battle. Once again, driving out the shogunate army quickly becomes something to dream about."
Kageaki"...And if, on top of this, the shogunate fleet intercepts the Philippine reinforcements at sea—"
Cannon"............"
Kageaki"Then survival comes first, occupation of Yamato afterward. Put it all together... I am not seeing so much room for your optimism."
Kageaki"Your view, Lieutenant Colonel?"
Cannon"Hmm. Well... I will grant it."
Kageaki"..."
Cannon"A fairly sound reading of the situation. If we began hostilities this instant, matters would very likely go as you say. A quick victory would be difficult."
Kageaki"If you want me to turn those poor odds into good ones, Lieutenant Colonel... I must inform you that your selection has gone completely wrong."

キャノン「そう、だから我々は短期決戦を目指す。 　そして……実現するだろう」
景明「六波羅が地の利を盾に取り、勝つよりも 負けない・・・・戦いに徹したとしても？」
キャノン「彼らの性質的に、なかなかその決断は下せ ないと思うが？」
景明「祖国を裏切り、貴方がたの軍門にひとまず 屈する恥辱にも耐えた六波羅です。 　必要とあらばどんな手段も躊躇いますまい」
キャノン「……なるほど」
景明「自分が六波羅の将帥であれば、貴方がたの 攻勢を支える一方で横須賀に兵を回します。 　横須賀は進駐軍にとって補給の要……」
景明「ここを潰されれば、貴方がたの行動限界は 更に早まります。……物資は現地調達するに も限度がある。 　動ける間に普陀楽を陥とすのはまず、無理」
景明「だからといって横須賀の防備を堅くすれば、 決戦の兵力が不足する。 　やはり短時日の内に幕府軍を駆逐するなど 夢物語になってしまう」
景明「……この上もし、フィリピンからの援軍が 海上で幕府艦隊に要撃されるようなことでも あれば――」
キャノン「…………」
景明「貴方がたは大和占領どころか、生き延びる 方法をまず考えなくてはならない境遇に陥る。 　総じて……進駐軍はそう楽観できる状況に はないと、自分には思えるのです」
景明「如何か。中佐殿」
キャノン「ふむ。 　まぁ……認めるさ」
景明「……」
キャノン「全般状況を鑑みるに、まずまず妥当な分析 だ。仮にいま、戦争の火蓋を切って落とせば、 君の言うように事態が推移する可能性は高い。 　我々が短期間で勝利を掴むのは困難だ」
景明「その薄い勝算を濃くするために自分が求め られているのなら、中佐殿……お眼鏡違いも 甚だしいと答えるほかありませんが」
